title: The recommendation, its reasons and its cost and effect have no table, no operation and no vocabulary in any source
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E5-012, story, data table, endpoints table); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-12 (systems 'Workbench, Model gateway'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.12.2 and A2.12.3.1 (R-LIT-36, BR-S4-012); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.1 and T-A.1; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4: 2 tables, 5 operations, 0 events, 0 jobs, 1 workflow)
section: RWB-S4-E5012-APP sections 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.8, 13, 19; RWB-S4-E5012-CON sections 1, 2, 3, 7 (AC1, AC5), 8 (BR1, BR7, BR11), 11, 12.1, 12.2, 12.7, 12.8, 13, 19; the metadata rows and the two fragments
description: Four values the step needs are fixed by no source. (1) The home of the proposal: the ownership rows of rwb-litigation name only hearing and legal_action as its tables, and neither carries a proposed step, a reason, a cost or an effect; the legacy data table names recovery_case, task, legal_action, notice, decision_log_entry and rule_row and no recommendation entity. (2) The interface: of the five owned operations of rwb-litigation none proposes a step, and the legacy endpoints table names only the notice approval and the legal-action create. (3) The vocabulary of the proposed step: no source lists the steps a proposal may name, no list of values carries them and no reference table is named, so the vocabulary cannot be written as a constant. (4) The agent row: the FSD names the Model gateway as an integration point and R-LIT-36 says the agent proposes the step with its cost and effect, but no source names an operation, an element or a field identifier, and DP-20 with its C RWB-P10-TE013-CON is not in the pattern set the plan gives this key, while the metadata C row is None.
evidence: Context pack 'Tables (2) - hearing, legal_action', 'REST operations provided (5)', 'Events (0)', 'Jobs (0)', 'Workflows (1) - LitigationWorkflow'. Legacy RWB-E5-012 data table: recovery_case, task, legal_action, notice, decision_log_entry, rule_row, and no recommendation row. Legacy endpoints: POST /api/recovery/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve and POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions only. FSD S4 A2.12.2 'Integration points. Workbench, Model gateway'. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-36 action 'The agent proposes the step with its cost and effect, and routes it to the approver'. Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-20 'Agent client - rwb-agent contract - C RWB-P10-TE013-CON'; the pattern sets of both stories are DP03, DP13, DP19 and both C rows are None.
area: contract; data model; rule and agent integration
owner_role: Solution architect of S4 with the P10 architect and the business owner of S4
proposed: The proposal is not a business row: it is a view of the decision record answered on API-S4-003, with the step vocabulary as a versioned reference value, and the cost and effect are read on rwb-agent's contract under DP-20 with the rule as fallback. No sixth operation is added to the five of TSD S4 T-A.1 and the C row stays None until D1 or the plan owner rules otherwise.

title: The trigger of the step, the officer task raise and the generation hold have no event and no published operation
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E5-012 AC1 to AC3 and data table (task, DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.12.2 (step 1 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'), A2.12.4.4 (system background events None); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md rows R-LIT-04, R-LIT-16, R-LIT-36; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T4, T5.2, T5.3; _work/msr/context/S4.md (Events (0); Workflows (1) LitigationWorkflow)
section: RWB-S4-E5012-APP sections 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 12.8, 13; RWB-S4-E5012-CON sections 2, 3, 7 (AC2, AC3), 8 (BR3), 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.5, 19; the events_published and events_consumed keys of both fragments
description: Three readings collide. (1) The trigger: the FSD describes the trigger of the feature as 'a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer', the rules name an event for each outcome (TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN, PACK_COMPLETE, SETTLEMENT_PROPOSED), and the ownership rows give rwb-litigation zero events while the FSD A2.12.4.4 declares no system background event. (2) The task raise: R-LIT-04 and R-LIT-16 'raise a task to the litigation officer', but the task row DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026 is P3's and no source states how the request crosses to rwb-case or names the operation. (3) The hold of generation: R-LIT-04 holds the notice generation, which is a notice behaviour of FEAT-LIT-01 and of rwb-comms (P6), and no source says whether the hold is a comms call, a case flag or an answer; the FSD and the legacy story both stay silent.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.12.2 step 1 'Receives its trigger: a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer'; FSD S4 A2.12.4.4 'None - No background event'. Context pack 'Events (0) - None' and 'Jobs (0) - None'. TSD S4 T5.2 'Calls go through the published Java interfaces: P3 for the case ... P6 for notices' with no operation named; TSD S4 T5.3 'Events - None'. Legacy data table: task 'id, case_id, task_code, element_type, discretion, status and 4 more' with DF-WRK-017 to DF-WRK-026. Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04 action 'Hold generation and raise a task to the litigation officer'.
owner_role: Solution architect of S4 with the P3 and P6 architects
proposed: The trigger is read as the pack-complete and template-withdrawn signals raised by this service's own pack and defect-list steps and delivered to the workflow; no Kafka topic, consumer group or inbox is declared. The officer task, the case-stage timer and the case move are answered to rwb-case in one stage outcome, and the generation hold is answered to rwb-comms with the rule and its version.

title: The template status of R-LIT-04 and the pack element of R-LIT-16 have no owner field, no identifier and no published operation
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-LIT-04 (condition template_status = withdrawn) and R-LIT-16 (condition every defect list item present); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md RWB-E5-012 data table (notice, DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023, 'and 3 more'); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v2.md T3.1 (legal_action, hearing only), T3.2 (LOV lists), T5.2; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.12.3.1; _work/msr/context/S4.md (ownership rows of S4)
description: R-LIT-04 fires on 'template_status = withdrawn' and R-LIT-16 on 'every defect list item present', and neither value has a home in the sources read for this key. The notice row DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023 belongs to rwb-comms and the legacy table names six of its nine fields, so the template status is not shown to be one of them and no field identifier is published for it; the TSD S4 T3.1 declares only legal_action and hearing for this service and no template or document entity at all. The defect list item is a document of the pack, which TSD S4 T5.2 gives to P5, and the pack index has no published element, no field identifier and no operation name in any source read for this key.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-04 condition 'template_status = withdrawn', R-LIT-16 condition 'every defect list item present'. FSD S4 A2.12.3.1 gives both rules and BR-S4-012 ('read from reference data with its version'). Legacy data table: notice 'id, case_id, document_id, notice_type, sent_date, barcode and 3 more' with DF-LEG-015 to DF-LEG-023. TSD S4 T3.1 declares legal_action and hearing only; T3.2 lists LOV-LEGAL-TYPE, LOV-LEGAL-STATUS, LOV-HEARING, LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME with no template or defect list value. TSD S4 T5.2 'P5 for documents' with no operation named.
owner_role: Solution architect of S4 with the P5 and P6 architects and the business owner of S4
proposed: The template status is read on rwb-comms' notice contract as part of the notice answer and its field identifier carries the placeholder; the pack index is read on rwb-document's contract with the defect list items and carries the placeholder on its element and operation name. When a fact is absent, the rule does not fire, nothing is written and no move is answered.

title: The legacy master carries no requirement identifier for RWB-E5-012, so both stories trace to the feature and one nearest module requirement
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md heading RWB-E5-012 (metadata rows Epic, Module, Feature FEAT-LIT-12, Process, Priority, Depends on FEAT-LIT-11, Decision - no requirement row); _work/msr/plan/legacy_index.json entry RWB-E5-012 with reqs = []; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md row FEAT-LIT-12; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md 'Requirements served' REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010
section: Sections 2 and 18 of both stories and the reqs key of both fragments
description: The legacy story RWB-E5-012 carries no REQ identifier: its metadata table names the feature FEAT-LIT-12 and the prerequisite FEAT-LIT-11 and no requirement row, the run's legacy index records an empty requirement list, and the Epics 3 to 8 specification gives the feature one row and no requirement. The FSD S4 requirements table names REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 and none of them names the next-step recommendation; the nearest is REQ-S4-005, 'Court state, hearing dates, deadlines and fees are tracked on the case without a person reading an email', whose facts the step reads. Both stories therefore carry the placeholder in place of a requirement ID, state the nearest reading, and keep the PRD column Pending (C1).
evidence: The metadata table of RWB-E5-012 has seven rows and no requirement row; the legacy index records reqs: [] for the key; FSD S4 v3 'Requirements served' lists REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010 and none names a recommendation; the Epics 3 to 8 specification row for FEAT-LIT-12 gives Epic E5, Module S4, Kind System, primary role 'Runs unattended', systems 'Workbench, Model gateway', depends on FEAT-LIT-11.
owner_role: Business analyst of S4 and the PRD owner of EP05
proposed: Both stories trace to FEAT-LIT-12 with the nearest reading REQ-S4-005 stated in section 18, the reqs key stays empty in both fragments, and the PRD column stays Pending (C1) until the Epics 3 to 8 PRD adds an identifier.

title: The rule package that decides the three rules is a consumed contract of another service with no dependency row and no pattern in the set
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md R-LIT-04, R-LIT-16, R-LIT-36; _work/msr/context/S4.md (DP table row DP-04 and the rule governance block of Temporal and Drools slide 11); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3.md A2.12.3.1; the metadata rows of RWB-S4-E5012-APP and RWB-S4-E5012-CON (Contract dependencies None; patterns DP03, DP13, DP19)
description: The step cannot propose anything without the LITIGATION package of rwb-decision at its version in force, because the three rules and their conditions are rows of that package. In the target the package is authored, tested and approved in rwb-decision (P7) and the runtime is embedded per service, which the DP table carries as DP-04 with H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON and C RWB-P7-E1073-CON. DP-04 is not in the pattern set of this key, no such platform or service contract story is in the dependencies the plan gives this slice, and the metadata rows say Contract dependencies None, so the package read is a consumed contract that no row declares.
evidence: Context pack DP table: short form 'DP-04 embedded Drools + rule packages from rwb-decision'; full table row 'DP-04 ... H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON'. Temporal and Drools slide 11: 'RULE GOVERNANCE (rwb-decision, P7): rule models + central ledger, approve, publish EV-30, seal decision records'. FSD S4 A2.12.3.1 gives R-LIT-04, R-LIT-16, R-LIT-36 and BR-S4-012 'read from reference data with its version'. The patterns of both stories are DP03, DP13, DP19 and both H lists name only RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON beside the CON.
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision architect with the solution architect of S4
proposed: The LITIGATION package is consumed from rwb-decision as a non-blocking contract with its fake at its version in force, the embedded runtime stays a service-template capability, and neither story declares a rule row, a package or a rule version of its own; if a C row is later required, only the Dependency Map and the metadata rows change.
